title: Repros and checks that import the query log capture write to an isolated spool, never the clone's own
goal: Answers the SP-mlemdqbn retrospective: a bug repro that imported ql_capture with CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA set but not CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT fell back to the clone's _cache/querylog spool and wrote a junk work row there, removed by hand. bl_base.run_check runs every check and repro with an isolated query log home (CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA and CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT pointing at a temporary directory, or the DISABLED marker), so no check or repro adds rows to the real spool; kb/_self/backlog.md and kb/_self/querylog.md say so.

run: import sys;sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import bl_base;ok,code,out=bl_base.run_check(".",{"run":["python3","-c","import os,sys;d=os.environ.get(\"CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA\",\"\");sys.exit(0 if d and os.environ.get(\"CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT\") and \"_cache\" not in d else 1)"]});print("check runs with an isolated query log home:",ok);sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

gates.question: How does bl_base.run_check give every check and repro an isolated query log home? tempdir: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA set to a fresh temporary directory (config mode local) and CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT to the clone, so capture still runs and writes there, then the directory is deleted; off: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA set to a temporary directory holding the DISABLED marker, so capture writes nothing. A check that sets its own CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA keeps its own in both.
